nodes.text: 8. And in the third book the same [author] mentions Moses, saying the following: "Next came Jannes and Jambres, Egyptian sacred scribes, men judged to be second to none in magic, at the time when the Jews were being driven out of Egypt. It was they, at any rate, whom the people of Egypt thought fit to stand against Musaeus, who led the Jews, a man who had proved most powerful in praying to God; and of the calamities which Musaeus brought on Egypt they were seen to be able to undo the most violent." Through these [words] Numenius bears witness both to the extraordinary wonders performed by Moses and to Moses himself as one dear to God.
